# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1324
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1324
- **Title**: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-notify-coverage` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T15:58:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:50:34Z

## PR Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1324
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1324
- **Title**: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-notify-coverage` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T15:58:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:50:34Z

## PR Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

- **PR #**: 1324
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1324
- **Title**: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1319-notify-coverage` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T15:58:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:50:34Z

## PR Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. - **Branch**: `fix/1319-notify-coverage` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +59
- **Deletions**: -10
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T15:58:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T16:50:34Z

## PR Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

## PR Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).

- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

# pr-1324: fix(1319): route paging history notifies through the guarded bridge (follow-up to #1320)

## Description

Follow-up to #1320, finishing its review's IMPORTANT thread (PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6piPiu, «_notify chokepoint not total — main-body paging methods still notify directly»). Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

## Regression test (failing-first, deterministic)

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart`: **9/9 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite including the originally-red `UT-oversized-windowed`).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files: only the pre-existing unrelated info (`use_null_aware_elements`, present on pristine main).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries pre-existing format dirt on main (verified against the stashed pristine tree) — whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320.

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

## Delivered vs remaining

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. Not done (deliberate): the three cosmetic suggestion threads on #1320 (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) are left for owner curation; the remaining ~11 direct `notifyListeners()` call sites in the class body are synchronous and not reachable by this race.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. Issue #1319 itself is already closed by #1320 — this PR only extends the same fix to the paths that thread enumerated; nothing to auto-close.

## What was missed

`AgentService`'s class body bypassed the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge in the three async history-paging continuations:

- `loadOlderHistory()` — notifies at 1792, 1804, 1808, and the `finally` at 1811
- `loadNewerHistory()` — notifies at 1833, 1874, 1877, and the `finally` at 1880
- `jumpToMessage()` — notifies at 1909 and the `finally` at 1923

Each suspends on real file I/O between notifications, and `dispose()` never bumps `_loadGeneration`, so the `gen != _loadGeneration` guards pass after dispose and the tail/`finally` `notifyListeners()` lands on the dead ChangeNotifier — the identical crash class #1320 fixed for the background count, reachable when a scroll-triggered page-in is in flight at a session switch or test teardown.

## Fix

All ten paging notify sites routed through the guarded `_notify()` bridge — mechanical `notifyListeners()` → `_notify()` (20 +/- in the file: 10 swaps), zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` calls in the class body are synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation — outside this race's reach, left untouched per the thread's own scope.

`UT-dispose-race-paging` in `session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` (second test, same gated-fixture pattern as #1320's): freezes the next ranged read, starts `loadOlderHistory()` (100 records above the tail window), disposes the service mid-read, releases the gate. The continuation resumes post-dispose, the gen guard passes, and the `finally` notify fires:

- **Unpatched (fresh main, verified before this patch):** RED — `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners → AgentService.loadOlderHistory (agent_service.dart:1811)` "A AgentService was used after being disposed", surfaced deterministically via `await pageIn` (no zone-timing dependence).
- **Patched:** green.

Same lane-host constraints as #1320 — system dart/flutter toolchain unreliable (EPERM engine-stamp writes / VM SIGKILL), so the gates ran on the temp Flutter 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 SDK copy with a fleet pub-cache:

CI is the real gate per fleet policy — no workflows dispatched or rerunned from this lane.

Delivered: the ten paging sites guarded, deterministic failing-first regression for the paging route, targeted suites green. Remaining (owner/SM): merge-train CI. blocks.text:
There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... Actually: `abort(); await waitForIdle();` — `abort()` is called synchronously when the future starts executing (which happens synchronously when `reconfigure` is invoked — async function bodies run synchronously until the first await). So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? After the run loop finishes and `agent_end` listeners settle. That's definitely multiple event-loop turns after `reconfigure()` is invoked.

But my test calls `service.dispose()` synchronously right after invoking `reconfigure`. If the drain could complete before dispose, the notify would happen while alive (no crash, test vacuously green). Given microtask timing: dispose runs synchronously before ANY microtask, so dispose definitely lands while the drain is in flight. Deterministic.

blocks.text:
There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... Actually: `abort(); await waitForIdle();` — `abort()` is called synchronously when the future starts executing (which happens synchronously when `reconfigure` is invoked — async function bodies run synchronously until the first await). So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? After the run loop finishes and `agent_end` listeners settle. That's definitely multiple event-loop turns after `reconfigure()` is invoked.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:

4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.

blocks.text:
There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? messages.preview: The `_hungResponse()` pattern exists. Let me check `_disposeService`, the `error` setter, and how agent event listeners notify:

blocks.text:
There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... Actually: `abort(); await waitForIdle();` — `abort()` is called synchronously when the future starts executing (which happens synchronously when `reconfigure` is invoked — async function bodies run synchronously until the first await). So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? After the run loop finishes and `agent_end` listeners settle. That's definitely multiple event-loop turns after `reconfigure()` is invoked.

But my test calls `service.dispose()` synchronously right after invoking `reconfigure`. If the drain could complete before dispose, the notify would happen while alive (no crash, test vacuously green). Given microtask timing: dispose runs synchronously before ANY microtask, so dispose definitely lands while the drain is in flight. Deterministic. 

But wait — there's a subtlety: does `sendText` need the session? In the race test, the service is constructed via `_service(tmp.path, gated)` and opened through the manager. But I could keep the reconfigure test simpler: construct the service directly with a hung stream function (like agent_service_test.dart does with MemoryExecutionEnv), no session file needed. `sendText` on an initialized service starts a new session lazily. But `_session?.appendModelChange` in reconfigure is guarded by try/on Object. And sessionsRoot '/sessions' with MemoryExecutionEnv works in agent_service_test.dart.

Hmm, but hold on — does the repo's `JsonlSessionRepo` need a real fs? The agent_service_test uses `sessionsRoot: '/sessions'` with MemoryExecutionEnv and no repo? Let me check the AgentService constructor defaults... The existing test constructs `AgentService(agent: ..., env: env, sessionsRoot: '/sessions')` without a repo. OK so for the reconfigure test, I can use a similar minimal setup.

But there's one thing to check: `service.dispose()` during an active run — does `_disposeService()` abort the run? Let me check `_disposeService` in agent_service_lifecycle.dart. If dispose aborts the active run too, that's fine — the ordering still holds.

Also, is `notifyListeners` at 2312 the ONLY notify in the reconfigure path? The `error = null;` setter before it — `error` setter may notify. Let me check the `error` setter. Also `abort()` → agent state changes → listeners on agent state? The service listens to agent events and notifies on stream events — but those flow through the events part-file. The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:

2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... Actually: `abort(); await waitForIdle();` — `abort()` is called synchronously when the future starts executing (which happens synchronously when `reconfigure` is invoked — async function bodies run synchronously until the first await). So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? After the run loop finishes and `agent_end` listeners settle. That's definitely multiple event-loop turns after `reconfigure()` is invoked.

But my test calls `service.dispose()` synchronously right after invoking `reconfigure`. If the drain could complete before dispose, the notify would happen while alive (no crash, test vacuously green). Given microtask timing: dispose runs synchronously before ANY microtask, so dispose definitely lands while the drain is in flight. Deterministic.

There's an existing `_hungResponse()` pattern in `agent_service_test.dart` — a stream that stays open until the cancel token fires. I can reuse this pattern in the race test.

The test plan for `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`:
1. Create service with a `_hungResponse`-style stream function.
2. `service.initialize()`.
3. `final run = service.sendText('hi');` — starts a streaming run (unawaited).
4. Wait a tick for the run to be active (`_agent.state.isStreaming`).
5. `final switchOver = service.reconfigure(_config)` — unawaited. This calls `abort()` (cancels the token → hung stream ends with aborted error) and awaits `waitForIdle()`.
6. `service.dispose();` while the drain is still in flight (i.e., before `waitForIdle()` completes).
7. `await switchOver;` — the drain completes, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the direct `notifyListeners()` at 2312 fires on the disposed notifier → on unpatched code this throws "A AgentService was used after being disposed" and `await switchOver` fails the test.

Ordering considerations:
- `abort()` cancels the token synchronously (cancel source). The `onCancel` callback pushes an ErrorEvent and ends the stream — but that's async (`.then`), so the run drain takes at least a microtask/event-loop turn. But wait — could the drain complete BEFORE dispose() runs? `dispose()` is called synchronously right after `service.reconfigure(...)` returns a future. The `reconfigure` body up to `await waitForIdle()` runs synchronously until the first await... Actually: `abort(); await waitForIdle();` — `abort()` is called synchronously when the future starts executing (which happens synchronously when `reconfigure` is invoked — async function bodies run synchronously until the first await). So `abort()` runs synchronously, `waitForIdle()` future is obtained; `await` suspends.

The cancel token's `onCancel.then(...)` fires in a later microtask. Then events are pushed, stream drains, run completes → `completer.future` resolves. When does `_activeRun.completer` complete? After the run loop finishes and `agent_end` listeners settle. That's definitely multiple event-loop turns after `reconfigure()` is invoked.

Force push is blocked. Alternative: keep the remote WIP commit as-is (identical content is already on the PR head) and simply reset my local branch to origin — no push needed at all. The content is already on the remote; validation is presumably already running on 081d1f9ea (a NEW head after the red 5943fc967, satisfying thread 3's "red yields the slot — a NEW head re-runs validation").

But the commit message "pr-1324 WIP auto-save 2026-10-06T17-06-44" is what the PR shows. Hmm. Can I push a NEW commit on top instead (a no-op or a comment commit)? That wouldn't fix the WIP message.

Options:
1. Accept the WIP message on the head commit — content is correct, validation runs. The PR shows an untidy commit message.
2. Push a follow-up empty commit with the proper message — noise.
3. Try `git push` non-force after resetting local to remote, then... no.

Actually — wait. Is there another lane convention? The remote got the WIP auto-save pushed automatically by the lane harness. The message churn isn't worth fighting the guard. But hold on — maybe I can push my clean commit as a NEW head on top of origin's WIP commit? That would duplicate the diff... no, my commit's parent is 5943fc967; pushing it would conflict.

Cleanest available: reset local to origin/fix/1319-notify-coverage (the auto-save commit), leaving the branch consistent. The PR head already contains all fixes with identical tree. Thread 3's requirement (new head → validation re-runs) is already satisfied by 081d1f9ea being pushed.

Hmm, but actually let me reconsider: is a normal (non-force) push of something possible? What about creating a proper commit on top of the WIP commit that's empty except... no — an empty "reword" isn't possible without rewrite.

Actually, let me check if there's a merge-trigger/machine-merge bot that squashes PR commits on merge (many fleets squash). Looking at the git log: merged PRs show as single commits like "fix(1319): drop notifications landing on a disposed AgentService (#1320)" — the "(#1320)" suffix pattern indicates SQUASH-MERGE. So individual commit messages on the branch don't matter — the squash commit message comes from the PR title, not the commit. The WIP commit message is cosmetic and disappears at squash-merge.

Decision: keep the remote head as-is (identical content). Reset local branch to match origin so the lane is consistent. Note this in the response.

Actually wait — one more consideration: my local branch has the amended commit. If the lane auto-save runs again and pushes, it would push 3302e1661 on top of remote 081d1f9ea → divergence. Better to reset local to origin now.

# PR #1324 rework — review follow-up fixes pushed

## Issues/Notes

Open threads addressed on head `081d1f9ea` (branch `fix/1319-notify-coverage`):

1. **IMPORTANT (automated review, thread 2)** — the PR description's claim that all remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites are "synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation" was inaccurate for `reconfigure()`: its notify at `agent_service.dart:2312` runs **after `await waitForIdle()`** (the abort-drain of the in-flight run). A `dispose()` landing during the drain put the #1319 crash class right back in reach.
2. **SUGGESTION (inline thread 1, `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6pj6eP`)** — `UT-dispose-race-paging` only proved absence-of-throw; the completed-continuation end state was not pinned.
3. **Validation CI red on head `5943fc967` (thread 3)** — red head predates this push; the new head re-runs validation (no `ci_failures.md`/log was provided in `input/`, so no separate CI root cause to fix; the lane's own targeted gates all pass, see Test Coverage).

## Approach

- **`reconfigure()` (one-line fix + comment):** routed the post-await notify through the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge — the exact mechanism the PR already applied to the ten paging sites. Zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites were re-audited one by one and are all genuinely synchronous (no intervening `await`): `setApprovalMode`, `setSkillsAccess`, `setToolEnabled`, the `sendText`/`sendAttachments`/`sendImage` early-return branches, `_notify()` itself, and the relay `reconfigure` override (its tail notify follows a non-awaited `dispatch`). The part-file extensions already route through `_notify()`. No other post-await notify remains in `AgentService`.

{"content":"# PR #1324 rework — review follow-up fixes pushed

## Issues/Notes

Open threads addressed on head `081d1f9ea` (branch `fix/1319-notify-coverage`):

1. **IMPORTANT (automated review, thread 2)** — the PR description's claim that all remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites are "synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation" was inaccurate for `reconfigure()`: its notify at `agent_service.dart:2312` runs **after `await waitForIdle()`** (the abort-drain of the in-flight run). A `dispose()` landing during the drain put the #1319 crash class right back in reach.
2. **SUGGESTION (inline thread 1, `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6pj6eP`)** — `UT-dispose-race-paging` only proved absence-of-throw; the completed-continuation end state was not pinned.
3. **Validation CI red on head `5943fc967` (thread 3)** — red head predates this push; the new head re-runs validation (no `ci_failures.md`/log was provided in `input/`, so no separate CI root cause to fix; the lane's own targeted gates all pass, see Test Coverage).

## Approach

- **`reconfigure()` (one-line fix + comment):** routed the post-await notify through the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge — the exact mechanism the PR already applied to the ten paging sites. Zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites were re-audited one by one and are all genuinely synchronous (no intervening `await`): `setApprovalMode`, `setSkillsAccess`, `setToolEnabled`, the `sendText`/`sendAttachments`/`sendImage` early-return branches, `_notify()` itself, and the relay `reconfigure` override (its tail notify follows a non-awaited `dispatch`). The part-file extensions already route through `_notify()`. No other post-await notify remains in `AgentService`.
- **`UT-dispose-race-paging` (test-only):** added `expect(service.messages, hasLength(300));` after `await pageIn` plus a contract comment covering the reviewer's caveat (if `dispose()` ever starts bumping `_loadGeneration`, the continuation bails at the gen guard without notifying and this assertion forces the contract comment to be updated instead of the test going vacuously green).
- **New `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure` regression test (TDD, failing-first):** a hung stream function (the `agent_service_test` `_hungResponse` pattern) keeps a run genuinely in flight; `reconfigure()` aborts it and suspends inside `waitForIdle()`; `dispose()` lands inside the drain; `await switchOver` then reproduces the crash. **Verified RED on the unpatched tree** — `A AgentService was used after being disposed` at `agent_service.dart:2312` in `AgentService.reconfigure`, exactly the flagged line — then GREEN after the one-line fix.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — `reconfigure()` tail notify → `_notify()` (+ explanatory comment).
- `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` — `hasLength(300)` end-state assertion in `UT-dispose-race-paging`; new `_createHungAgent()` helper; new `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure` test.

Pushed as head `081d1f9ea` on `fix/1319-notify-coverage` (this validation re-run is the thread-3 action; the lane's auto-save left the head commit message as `pr-1324 WIP auto-save 2026-10-06T17-06-44` — content is the rework commit, tree `0363d238`).

## Test Coverage

- `flutter test test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart test/session_oversized_windowed_test.dart` → **10/10 pass** (both dispose-race tests + the full oversized-windowed suite).
- New `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure`: proven failing-first on the unpatched production code, green after the fix.
- `agent_service` family regression net — `agent_service_test`, `agent_service_windowed`, `relay_agent_service`, `app_config`, `runs_helpers`, `session_load`, `thinking`, `timeout`, `tool_floor`, `rate_limit`, `secrets_merge`, `js_app_error_delivery`, `memory_user_scope`, `task_completion_wake`, `compaction_it` → **183 pass, 0 fail** (one earlier "failure" was a mistyped suite filename in the runner invocation, re-run correctly).
- `flutter analyze` on both changed files → only the pre-existing `use_null_aware_elements` info (`agent_service.dart:1865`, present on pristine main, untouched).
- `dart format`: test file clean; `agent_service.dart` carries the pre-existing main format dirt (whole-file reformat deliberately out of scope, same call as #1320).

Merge-train CI remains the real gate per fleet policy. The three cosmetic #1320 suggestion threads (gate-hit counter, idempotent dispose, shared fixtures) remain deliberately out of scope for owner curation, as does the `bump _loadGeneration`-in-`dispose()` alternative floated on #1320.

{"content":"# PR #1324 rework — review follow-up fixes pushed

## Issues/Notes

Open threads addressed on head `081d1f9ea` (branch `fix/1319-notify-coverage`):

1. **IMPORTANT (automated review, thread 2)** — the PR description's claim that all remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites are "synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation" was inaccurate for `reconfigure()`: its notify at `agent_service.dart:2312` runs **after `await waitForIdle()`** (the abort-drain of the in-flight run). A `dispose()` landing during the drain put the #1319 crash class right back in reach.
2. **SUGGESTION (inline thread 1, `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6pj6eP`)** — `UT-dispose-race-paging` only proved absence-of-throw; the completed-continuation end state was not pinned.
3. **Validation CI red on head `5943fc967` (thread 3)** — red head predates this push; the new head re-runs validation (no `ci_failures.md`/log was provided in `input/`, so no separate CI root cause to fix; the lane's own targeted gates all pass, see Test Coverage).

## Approach

- **`reconfigure()` (one-line fix + comment):** routed the post-await notify through the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge — the exact mechanism the PR already applied to the ten paging sites. Zero behavior change for live services. The remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites were re-audited one by one and are all genuinely synchronous (no intervening `await`): `setApprovalMode`, `setSkillsAccess`, `setToolEnabled`, the `sendText`/`sendAttachments`/`sendImage` early-return branches, `_notify()` itself, and the relay `reconfigure` override (its tail notify follows a non-awaited `dispatch`). The part-file extensions already route through `_notify()`. No other post-await notify remains in `AgentService`.
- **`UT-dispose-race-paging` (test-only):** added `expect(service.messages, hasLength(300));` after `await pageIn` plus a contract comment covering the reviewer's caveat (if `dispose()` ever starts bumping `_loadGeneration`, the continuation bails at the gen guard without notifying and this assertion forces the contract comment to be updated instead of the test going vacuously green).
- **New `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure` regression test (TDD, failing-first):** a hung stream function (the `agent_service_test` `_hungResponse` pattern) keeps a run genuinely in flight; `reconfigure()` aborts it and suspends inside `waitForIdle()`; `dispose()` lands inside the drain; `await switchOver` then reproduces the crash. **Verified RED on the unpatched tree** — `A AgentService was used after being disposed` at `agent_service.dart:2312` in `AgentService.reconfigure`, exactly the flagged line — then GREEN after the one-line fix.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — `reconfigure()` tail notify → `_notify()` (+ explanatory comment).
- `flutter_app/test/session_open_dispose_race_test.dart` — `hasLength(300)` end-state assertion in `UT-dispose-race-paging`; new `_createHungAgent()` helper; new `UT-dispose-race-reconfigure` test.

Pushed as head `081d1f9ea` on `fix/1319-notify-coverage` (this validation re-run is the thread-3 action; the lane's auto-save left the head commit message as `pr-1324 WIP auto-save 2026-10-06T17-06-44` — content is the rework commit, tree `0363d238`).

- `agent_service` family regression net — `agent_service_test`, `agent_service_windowed`, `relay_agent_service`, `app_config`, `runs_helpers`, `session_load`, `thinking`, `timeout`, `tool_floor`, `rate_limit`, `secrets_merge`, `js_app_error_delivery`, `memory_user_scope`, `task_completion_wake`, `compaction_it` → **183 pass, 0 fail** (one earlier "failure" was a mistyped suite filename in the runner invocation, re-run correctly).

{"content":"# PR #1324 rework — review follow-up fixes pushed

## Issues/Notes

Open threads addressed on head `081d1f9ea` (branch `fix/1319-notify-coverage`):

1. **IMPORTANT (automated review, thread 2)** — the PR description's claim that all remaining direct `notifyListeners()` sites are "synchronous setters with no in-flight continuation" was inaccurate for `reconfigure()`: its notify at `agent_service.dart:2312` runs **after `await waitForIdle()`** (the abort-drain of the in-flight run). A `dispose()` landing during the drain put the #1319 crash class right back in reach.
2. **SUGGESTION (inline thread 1, `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6pj6eP`)** — `UT-dispose-race-paging` only proved absence-of-throw; the completed-continuation end state was not pinned.
3. **Validation CI red on head `5943fc967` (thread 3)** — red head predates this push; the new head re-runs validation (no `ci_failures.md`/log was provided in `input/`, so no separate CI root cause to fix; the lane's own targeted gates all pass, see Test Coverage).

## Approach

- **`reconfigure()` (one-line fix + comment):** routed the post-await notify through the `_disposed`-guarded `_notify()` bridge — the exact mechanism the PR already applied to the ten paging sites. Zero behavior change for live services.
